documents.title: Doc 75 - DECISION - Car 11 - Alleged contact with Car 8 at Turn 18 in Race 2
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 11 - Alleged contact with Car 8 at Turn 18 in Race 2

details.fact: Car 8 (Taponen) and Car 11 (Gladysz) collided at Turn 18.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. Car 11 (GLA) was attempting an inside overtake on Car 11 (TAP) at turn 18. TAP turned in earlier than normal as part of his defense thus squeezing GLA while still leaving him racing room. GLA did not have his front axle alongside TAP’s mirror prior to the apex which means that he had not won the corner. While this would ordinarily mean that he was responsible for any ensuing collision, the stewards determine that TAP’s defensive move was made late enough that he contributed to the collision. Under the circumstances, the Stewards do not find either driver to be wholly or predominantly responsible for the collision. Based on the totality of the circumstances, the Stewards elect to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 73 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - Leaving the track and gaining an advantage
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - Leaving the track and gaining an advantage

details.fact: Car 6 (De Palo) cut the chicane at Turn10 and gained lasting advantage against Car 28 (Barrichello).
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (d) of the FIA F3 Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video & GPS evidence. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that at the exit of the tunnel Car 6 (DEP) attempted to overtake Car 28 (BAR) at Turn 10. DEP cut the chicane and rejoined in front of BAR and retained the advantage. When a car leaves the track while fighting for or defending a position it is generally expected that they will concede the position. The Stewards determine that DEP left the track and gained a lasting advantage and therefore decide to impose the standard ten (10) seconds time penalty.

documents.title: Doc 70 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 23 - Out of position at Safety Car line 1
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 23 - Out of position at Safety Car line 1

details.fact: Car 23 (Shin) failed to enter the pit lane after being out of position at the first safety car line.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 37.8 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Stop and Go Penalty which is mandatory pursuant to Article 37.8 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. There are no penalty points associated with this infraction.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video and GPS evidence. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that Car 23 (SHI) was very slow after Turn 15 during the formation lap. He was passed by Car 28 (BAR). SHI did not re-establish the original grid starting order before reaching Safety Car Line 1 and proceeded to start the race from the grid rather than entering the pits and starting from the end of the pit lane as required by Article 37.8 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. The Stewards apply the mandatory Stop and Go penalty for the infraction.

documents.title: Doc 63 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 14 - Technical infringement
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 14 - Technical infringement

details.fact: The front push rod LH - CPL (part number: F32506D001) of car #14 was mounted on the right-hand side of the car and the front push rod RH - CPL (part number: F32506D002) was mounted on the left-hand side of the car.
details.infringement: Breach of Articles 1.5.3 and 17.1 of the FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations.
details.decision: Car 14 is disqualified from the Sprint Race classification. All other drivers move up in the classification.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 61) and the FIA Formula 3 Technical Delegate. During the hearing the team representative acknowledged that the facts as stated above are true and correct: specifically, that the front push rod LH - CPL (part number: F32506D001) of car #14 was mounted on the right-hand side of the car and the front push rod RH - CPL (part number: F32506D002) was mounted on the left- hand side of the car. The team representative disputed that these facts constitute a breach of the FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations. (For the sake of convenience any and all Article references hereinafter contained are with respect to the FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations.) While the Technical Delegate’s report included a reference to Article 1.5.2, it is not alleged that the parts in question were modified. They were not. The question at hand is whether the parts were installed on the wrong side of the car. The FIA Technical Delegate and the team representative both referred to the language of Article Article 1.5.3 and Article 17.1 The relevant part of Article 1.5.3 provides, “For the avoidance of doubt the original design and construction of the car must be maintained at all times.” Article 17.1 titled General Principles begins, “The complete car is divided into three types of parts. The parts are classified in the spare parts catalogue.” The stewards find that the “original design and construction of the car” is illuminated by Article 17.1. It is clear that the car is made up of parts and that the parts are specified in the spare parts catalogue. The front pushrod is depicted on page 006D of the spare parts catalogue which also includes line references to “front push rod LH – CPL” (part number: F32506D001) and “front push rod RH – CPL” (part number: F32506D002) are listed on page 006G of the catalogue. The Technical Delegate explained that the front push rod LH is meant to be installed on the left hand side of the car, and vice versa. The team’s contention is that “LH” and “RH” are not defined within the spare parts catalogue as “left side” and “right side” and that, in the absence of a formal definition, the matter is unclear, vague and easily subject to misinterpretation. Given the alleged ambiguity, they feel that the car is compliant notwithstanding the facts of the installation. The stewards acknowledge that references to left or right with respect to a race car are taken to mean left or right from the driver’s point of view. Having considered the matter extensively, the stewards determine that the abbreviations LH and RH, which are used extensively throughout the catalogue, and are so commonplace within the world at large as to not reasonably require express definition within the sophisticated world of Formula 3. Furthermore, if the team had any confusion about what the abbreviations meant they had ample opportunity to seek clarification from the Technical Delegate and they did not do so. The stewards also note that the lower front wishbones (part number: F32506G001 and F32506G002) to which these parts connect are also designated and labeled as LH and RH. The Technical Delegate confirmed that the wishbones were correctly installed on the expected left hand and right hand sides of the car. In this case, the team connected front pushrod LH to front lower wishbone RH, and vice versa. The team points out that regardless of a parts name, many part's can only successfully be installed on one side of the car. While that may be true, the stewards believe that even in face of alleged ambiguity or confusion, the team ought to notice that the parts that wind up on the right hand side of the car are designated RH, and that the parts that wind up on the left hand side of the car are designated LH. Accordingly, the stewards further determine the meaning of LH and RH should be clear to the team based on its overall experience with the car and its numerous parts over time. The stewards determine that the front push rod LH – CPL must be installed on the left hand side of the car and that the front push rod RH – CPL must be installed on the right hand side of the car. The stewards determine that Articles 1.5.3 and 17.1 of FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations have therefore been breached and that the standard penalty of a disqualification needs to be applied for such an infringement.

documents.title: Doc 58 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 20 - Resumption procedure infringement
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 20 - Resumption procedure infringement

details.fact: After the fifteen (15) second signal had been shown, one team member was touching Car 20 (Sharp) in the fast lane. SHA did not restart the race from the pit lane.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 43.5 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: A Stop & Go penalty in accordance with Article 39.3(d) of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. As the penalty was imposed after the race, it is converted to 30 seconds added to the elapsed race time of the Driver concerned in accordance with Article 39.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video and timing evidence. The Stewards summoned and heard the team representative (document 40). The Race was suspended and subsequently resumed in accordance with Article 43 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. During the restart procedure, after the fifteen (15) second signal had been shown, one team member was still touching SHA’s car in the fast lane. No team equipment was connected to the car. In accordance with Article 43.5 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations, SHA was therefore required to restart the race from the pit lane. The timing evidence showed that SHA did not restart the race from the pit lane. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determine that SHA failed to restart the race from the pit lane as required by Article 43.5. The mandatory penalty under Article 43.5 for this failure is a Stop & Go penalty in accordance with Article 39.3(d). As this penalty is imposed after the race, it is converted to 30 seconds added to the elapsed race time of SHA.

documents.title: Doc 52 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 5 - Causing a collision
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 5 - Causing a collision

details.fact: Car 5 (Slater) collided with Car 3 (Rivera) and at T6.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F3 Sporting Regulations. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 2 points
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. Car 5 (SLA) attempted an inside pass and collided with Car 3 (RIV) at the apex of Turn 6. SLA did not get far enough alongside by the apex to have established his rights in the corner. The stewards determine that SLA is wholly responsible for the collision and apply the standard penalty.

documents.title: Doc 51 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 8 - Causing a collision
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 8 - Causing a collision

details.fact: Car 8 (Taponen) collided with Car 3 (Rivera) and at T6 on Lap 1.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F3 Sporting Regulations. As the penalty could not be served in race, it will be converted to a 5 place grid drop at his next Feature Race. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 2 points
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. Car 8 (TAP), who had no overlap with Car 3 (RIV) at the turn in point for Turn 6, attempted an inside pass and collided with RIV at the apex. Notwithstanding the fact that TAP’s front axle became even with RIV’s mirror as the cars collided at the apex, the stewards determine that the move was so late and optimistic that TAP had not fairly won the corner. The stewards determine that TAP is wholly responsible for the collision and apply the standard penalty.

details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F3 Sporting Regulations. As the penalty could not be served in race, it will be converted to a 5 place grid drop for his next Feature Race. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 2 points
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. Car 26 (BEN) was trailing Car 30 (BHI) and had slight overlap with Car 19 (CHO) to his right while approaching Turn 6. documents.title: Doc 33 - DECISION - Car 16 - Allegedly leaving track and gaining an advantage
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 16 - Allegedly leaving track and gaining an advantage

details.fact: Car 16 (Del Pino) went off track at Turn 10 and rejoined in front of Car 28 (Barrichello).
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: No further action
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed video and GPS track map evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (Document 21). In the last minute of qualifying of Group A, Car 16 (DEP) cut the chicane at Turn 10 and rejoined in front of Car 28 (BAR) thus gaining a possible queuing advantage. The driver explained, and video confirmed, that he attempted to give the position back at T15. Under the circumstances, the stewards elect to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 32 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 23 - Failure of reattaching steering wheel
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 23 - Failure of reattaching steering wheel

details.fact: The Driver of Car 23 (Shin) did not reattach his steering wheel after vacating the car after the end of Qualifying.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 22.5 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: A fine of 500 Euros to be paid by the Team. In accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the ISC, fines shall be paid within forty‐eight hours of their notification by means of bank transfer to the FIA.
details.reason: The Stewards examined photo evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 27). Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that as advised by the Technical Delegate (document 26) the Driver of Car 23 (Shin) did not refit the steering wheel as required at the end of Qualifying.

documents.title: Doc 31 - DECISION - Car 8 - Alleged unsafe release
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 8 - Alleged unsafe release

details.fact: Car 8 (Taponen) was released nearly simultaneously with Car 4 (Stromsted) at the beginning of Qualifying Session A.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 28.12 (a) of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: No further action
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and team representatives (Documents 22 & 23). It is undisputed that Car 4 (STR), who had just been released into the fast lane, had to brake to avoid Car 8 (TAP). Having considered the matter extensively, the stewards determine that both cars were released nearly simultaneously with TAP moving before any wheel of STR’s car entered the fast lane. Unfortunately, there was a car in between the pair which hindered STR’s ability to notice that TAP was moving as well. This contributed to the cars being in close proximity before STR was able to react. The stewards further note that at the moment STR was being released, a television cameraman walked in between the crewmember releasing TAP and the front of TAP’s car, thus obscuring his vision of STR’s release and adding an element of distraction to the release process. Given the totality of these circumstances, the stewards do not find any fault with respect to the decision to release. To the extent that the situation was unsafe at all, it was predominantly attributable to the presence of the car between these two blocking the view on this tight pit lane and the actions of the cameraman. Accordingly, the stewards decide to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 30 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 4 - Impeding of Car 8
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 4 - Impeding of Car 8

details.fact: Car 4 (Stromsted) impeded Car 8 (Taponen) between Turns 3 and 4 during Qualifying Group A.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 31.6 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: A drop of three grid positions for both races at this Competition. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video, CCTV, GPS and timing evidence. They summoned and heard the Drivers and Team Representatives (Documents 24 & 25). Car 4 (STR) was on a cool down lap. After Turn 1, STR was warned by radio that a car on a push lap was approaching behind him. TAP caught STR at Turn 3, where TAP had to abort his push lap. During the hearing, the STR stated that he tried to move out of the way at both Turn 3 and Turn 4, and that TAP had aborted his lap too early. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that there was a speed difference of more than 100 km/h between the two cars at Turn 2 and at the beginning of Turn 3. Given the speed delta, the Stewards also conclude that TAP did not abort his push lap too early. Given the advance warning, the stewards believe that STR could have taken steps to have their interaction occur at a more favorable part of the track. Accordingly, the Stewards find that STR unnecessarily impeded TAP and impose the standard penalty for such an infringement in Qualifying.
